purpose: Can we compare two packing methods without confusing them with a busy day?
meaning: Compare B with A within each of three days, then average those paired differences. An additive day offset moves both methods together and cancels from their same-day comparison. Day is the blocking factor; the within-block contrast compares B with A on that same day.

definition.setting: A packing workshop plans two similar parcels on each of three days. Randomly assign the two methods within each day before measuring. For this teaching construction, method A takes 10−b, 10 and 10+b minutes; method B adds d−1, d and d+1 minutes. Slide the common shift d or the day offset b, and keep each day’s pair together.

signature.A: Method A packing time within a day, in minutes
signature.B: Method B packing time within that same day, in minutes
signature.d: Common constructed B−A shift in minutes
signature.b: Size of the additive day offset, in minutes
signature.d₁: B−A difference on day one, in minutes
signature.d₂: B−A difference on day two, in minutes
signature.d₃: B−A difference on day three, in minutes
signature.d̄: Mean of the three within-day B−A differences, in minutes

conditions: Every day contains both methods once. The displayed measurements are constructed and the assignment selector shows two fixed possible allocations, not a random sampler. The mean B−A is a descriptive contrast. Blocking cancels a shared additive day offset; it does not cancel treatment-by-day variation, validate randomization in actual data, establish causation or perform ANOVA. Use d from −4 to 4 and b from 0 to 4 minutes. Changes too small to survive the represented readings receive a precision state.
